apps.name: changedetection
apps._comment: DECISION (t_0b444f02): the instance's API and RSS tokens are redacted from the published artifact; a restored instance generates its own on first start. Why this option: it is the only one that needs no credential material anywhere outside the running instance, and it matches the behaviour the app already has for the other credential in this datastore - secret.txt is excluded from the archive for exactly the same reason (it is a credential and does not belong on a backup target), and the app's own store.py regenerates a missing api_access_token / rss_access_token on startup (store.py: 'Generate the URL access token for RSS feeds' / 'Generate the API access token'). Rejected alternatives: (a) restoring the SAME tokens from a SOPS-encrypted Secret at restore time - keeps one credential in two places and leaves the tokens in every older artifact, so it does not actually reduce the exposure; (b) accepting the exposure in writing - /mnt/nas-roms is a CIFS share that also holds Books, Movies, Music and roms, it is not a secret store, and api_access_token is a bearer token accepted on the WRITE routes too (DELETE /api/v1/watch/<uuid>), so this instance's only authentication would be readable by anyone with read access to the share. The redaction is fail-closed: if the member cannot be parsed, the redaction path is missing, the spec matches no member, or the token value turns up anywhere in the staged archive, the backup run FAILS and nothing is published. The verify step still compares the archived watch count against the live source.
